title: Impersonal verbs (il faut, il y a…)
summary: Impersonal verbs are only used with il, which means 'it' or 'there', never 'he': il faut, il pleut, il y a.
il faut + infinitive = you must / we must / it is necessary to: Il faut recycler le plastique. il ne faut pas = you mustn't: Il ne faut pas jeter les déchets par terre.
il faut + noun = you need: Il faut un passeport pour voyager. Past: il fallait; future: il faudra.
il y a = there is / there are: Il y a un cinéma en ville. Past description: il y avait; future: il y aura; negative: il n'y a pas de...
il y a + a length of time = ago: Je suis arrivé ici il y a deux ans.
Weather: il pleut, il neige, il fait beau / chaud / froid / mauvais, il y a du vent / du soleil. Past: il pleuvait, il faisait beau; future: il pleuvra, il fera chaud.
il est + adjective + de + infinitive = it is ... to ...: Il est important de manger équilibré. Il est difficile de trouver un emploi.
il vaut mieux + infinitive = it's better to: Il vaut mieux prendre le train.
il reste = there is / are ... left (always singular): Il reste deux places. il s'agit de = it's about: Dans ce livre, il s'agit d'une famille pauvre.

cards.front: What does il faut mean, and what follows it?
cards.back: It means 'you must / we must / it is necessary to' and never changes for the person. Followed by an infinitive: Il faut protéger l'environnement. Followed by a noun it means 'you need': Il faut un billet pour entrer.

cards.prompt: Il ___ éteindre la lumière quand on quitte une pièce.
cards.en: You must switch off the light when you leave a room.
cards.why: falloir is only used with il. In the present it is il faut, followed by an infinitive.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using il ne faut pas + infinitive.
cards.prompt: On ne doit pas fumer ici.
answers: Il ne faut pas fumer ici.
cards.why: il ne faut pas + infinitive means 'you mustn't': ne...pas goes round faut.

cards.prompt: Demain, il ___ partir à six heures pour prendre l'avion.
cards.en: Tomorrow we'll have to leave at six to catch the plane.
cards.why: The simple future of il faut is il faudra; demain points to the future.

cards.prompt: Quand j'étais à l'école primaire, il ___ porter un uniforme.
cards.en: When I was at primary school, we had to wear a uniform.
cards.why: A rule that applied over a period in the past → imperfect: il fallait.

cards.front: What do il y a, il y avait and il y aura mean?
cards.back: il y a = there is / there are; il y avait = there was / there were (imperfect, for description); il y aura = there will be. Negative: il n'y a pas de... With a length of time, il y a means 'ago': il y a trois ans = three years ago.

cards.prompt: Quand j'étais petit, il y ___ un parc derrière ma maison.
cards.en: When I was little, there was a park behind my house.
cards.why: Describing how things were in the past → imperfect: il y avait.

cards.prompt: L'année prochaine, il y ___ une nouvelle piscine dans notre ville.
cards.en: Next year there will be a new swimming pool in our town.
cards.why: The simple future of il y a is il y aura.

cards.prompt: Mes parents ont acheté cette maison ___ dix ans.
cards.en: My parents bought this house ten years ago.
cards.why: il y a + a length of time means 'ago'. It goes in front of the time (il y a dix ans), and the verb is in a past tense.

cards.front: How do you say: it's raining, it's snowing, the weather's nice, it's windy? And in the past and future?
cards.back: il pleut, il neige, il fait beau, il y a du vent (also il fait chaud / froid / mauvais, il y a du soleil / du brouillard). Past description: il pleuvait, il neigeait, il faisait beau. Future: il pleuvra, il neigera, il fera beau.

cards.prompt: Prends ton parapluie, il ___ depuis ce matin !
cards.en: Take your umbrella, it's been raining since this morning!
cards.why: depuis + present tense for something still going on: il pleut.

cards.prompt: Selon la météo, demain il ___ froid dans le nord.
cards.en: According to the forecast, tomorrow it will be cold in the north.
cards.why: Weather uses il fait + adjective; the simple future of faire is il fera.

cards.front: How does il est + adjective + de work?
cards.back: il est + adjective + de + infinitive = it is ... to ...: Il est important de dormir huit heures. Il est interdit de fumer. Il est difficile de trouver un petit boulot. de becomes d' before a vowel or silent h: Il est essentiel d'économiser l'énergie.

cards.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using il est + adjective + de + infinitive.
answers: Il est important de manger des fruits.
cards.en: It is important to eat fruit.
cards.why: il est + adjective + de + infinitive: Il est important de manger.

cards.front: What do il vaut mieux, il reste and il s'agit de mean?
cards.back: il vaut mieux + infinitive = it's better to: Il vaut mieux réserver à l'avance. il reste = there is / are ... left: Il reste trois billets. il s'agit de = it's about / it's a question of: Dans ce film, il s'agit d'une famille qui déménage. The subject is always il: never say 'ce film s'agit de'.

cards.prompt: Le concert est presque complet : il ne ___ que deux places.
cards.en: The concert is almost sold out: there are only two seats left.
cards.why: il reste is impersonal, so the verb stays singular even before a plural noun: il reste deux places, not 'restent'.

cards.prompt: Il ___ mieux prendre le train que la voiture en ville.
cards.en: It's better to take the train than the car in town.
cards.why: il vaut mieux + infinitive = it's better to (valoir in the present: il vaut). You will also meet the conditional il vaudrait mieux = it would be better to.

cards.prompt: Dans ce roman, il ___ d'une fille qui part vivre en Afrique.
cards.en: This novel is about a girl who goes to live in Africa.
cards.why: il s'agit de = it's about. It is only used with il, so the reflexive pronoun is s': il s'agit.
